utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning. May I, first of all, call for appearances as usual.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Slobodan Cvijetic for Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, and Eric Tully for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we begin, there is a matter which has become something of a concern which the Chamber thinks it should address frontally at this relatively early stage of the trial, and there have been a number of occasions when -- and this is -- whereas we're not singling out Mr. Pantelic, the -- in fact, the -- what we have identified as a problem has been usually as a consequence of his taking issue with the interpretation of the testimony of several of the witnesses as -- as provided by the interpreters. And Ms. Korner has usually responded that the way in which his interventions have been done are such as to, in effect, be telling the witnesses what to say. The -- on reflection the Chamber thinks it has been somewhat indulgent of counsel and consequently unfair to the interpreters, and we take this opportunity to remind all present, particularly counsel, that the process of interpretation is a different skill and different process from that of translation. And the effect of simultaneous interpretation is to provide a fair account, a sense of what the witness is saying and inevitably where, in this case, counsel and the witness speaks the same language, counsel or anybody else who -- who -- who speaks the same language as the witness may think that they would have done it differently. But we affirm our confidence in the integrity and ability of the interpreters to do their work, and the -- remind counsel that very often, to the extent that there is a difficulty, it is occasioned by the failure to allow time, an interval between question and answer for the interpreters to catch up. So the -- we will simply not hear counsel's interventions in the way that -- especially, Mr. Pantelic, has been proceeding in the past. So we trust that that is fully understood from this point on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The -- returning, in a similar vein, returning to this still not fully resolved question of these several documents on which counsel for the Defence have been relying and which we have indicated that the practical and sensible, in our view, method of approach is to put to the witnesses such portions of the documents as counsel is seeking to rely on or to challenge the witness, that, in order to facilitate the proper interpretation, counsel should make available to the interpreters copies of the documents in B/C/S so that they can, themselves, more easily and readily interpret the documents in terms of formulating -- assisting, counsel in formulating the questions that they're putting to the witness. Thank you. Finally, in this vein, counsel should remember that -- this goes for witnesses, too, to a certain extent, but again counsel, having the responsibility of leading the evidence, should remember to -- not to speak too quickly because, again, that complicates matters and makes it difficult for everybody concerned. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I appreciate your guide-lines and instructions regarding the way of how we should proceed in certain occasions. Just for the record, Your Honour, it is my duty to provide a full professional legal services to my client, and I will object on every occasion where I, in a situation to noticed -- to notice that important portion or word said by witness is not in transcript, due to, let's say, unintentional omission of our friends from interpretation. Working here for a quite long time, I appreciate, and I fully noted the efforts of our friends from interpretation. They are not robots, they are human beings. So in this highly -- I would say, highly stressful situation, where these kind of interpretation should be done, of course, unintentional omissions could be made. The advantage of number of lawyers for the Defence who are bilingual is that we can locate and catch these particular moments which is mostly not part of ability of the Prosecution or Trial Chamber. So this a criminal trial, and, of course, I will -- I'm -- it is not my intention to put in the mouth of witness particular portion of his testimony or to suggest him to testify along these lines. It is simply clarification of certain words or portions, which is necessary for us to have a clear and accurate transcript. As I said, this is a criminal trial, and our client's fate is in our hands. And sometimes when we, in general terms, realised that the quality of interpretation is not in accordance with the high standards of the interpretation within this Tribunal, personally I will react. I will react for the record. And I'm ready, Your Honours, to -- if something will arise to challenge, through audio tapes and comparing with the records to find -- to find the right solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I apologise for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge, and, indeed, the Bench does not disencourage counsel from drawing the Court's attention to possible mistakes. That was not what the Presiding Judge just said. What the Presiding Judge did say was that, to the extent in which errors made by the interpretation are due to the fact that counsel speak too fast or overlap with witnesses, then it is an invitation to counsel, once again, to speak slowly and not overlap, because, thereby, we may reduce the number of errors that the interpretation sometimes makes. That's all. But we do not, in any way, disencourage counsel on both sides to draw the attention to the Court if there are errors in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I announced that the Stanisic Defence has submission five minutes as a preliminary matter which we would like to share with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will speak in Serbian. Thank you very much. [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Stanisic's Defence is very concerned with the developments in this case, and we believe that it is our obligation to share our concerns with you and everybody else in the courtroom. We held a 65 ter conference last week. However, no progress was made, or virtually no progress at all. We still have a number of pending requests from the Prosecution and from the Defence which might have a direct impact on our preparations and the strategy of Defence in cross-examination. Unfortunately, the problem is not being reduced. It is becoming bigger. At the moment, we have reached a point where the integrity of the proceedings and the right to a fair trial guaranteed by the Statute is being put to the test in view of the Defence. Let me illustrate my statement. Yesterday, in the course of the trial, we had a warring situation in our view which also had an impact on the fairness of the trial. The facts are as follows. Our clients have been charged, amongst other things, that they did not take measures to prevent acts from the indictments or punish perpetrators and especially in Count 11 under age by abetting and aiding the commission of crimes by not undertaking the necessary measures in order to carry out investigations, the arrest of the perpetrators, by which he fostered the climate of non-punishability which included the investigation of such clients. This is what our clients have been charged with, especially Mr. Stanisic, in Counts 11(h) in the indictment in this case. In our view, the Defence has a legitimate right and it also has arguments and documents to present evidence which will directly and without any doubt refute the allegations, and confirm that the investigations, indeed, were carried out in keeping with the law and regulations, that there were was no discrimination with regard to the perpetrator or victim, and that there was certainly no purported investigations but, rather, procedures in -- in compliance with the law of the country where the crimes took place. It is not a mistake on the part of the Defence that the documents have not been translated. The fact is that the Prosecution disclosed them very late in the process. It is our position that the Defence has to be allowed to talk to the witness who is -- the Prosecutor who was directly involved in the criminal cases. We have to be given an opportunity to analyse all the documents to the last detail. We don't believe that perfunctory overviews are good enough, because here we are looking at concrete crimes, at concrete data, as to when, how, and where a certain crime happened, how a certain person lost their life. We are not dealing with arbitrary data as does the indictment. For example, in the indictment we have a number of examples where several people are mentioned as victims in different periods of time and in different places and as a result of different incidents and events. Therefore, I suggest that the Trial Chamber should allow the Zupljanin Defence, that is currently carrying out cross-examination, to analyse all the documents with the witness because the witness -- the documents show that the overall process was carried out in keeping with the law, and that's why each and every of the documents that are on the list is very important to prove our case. There is one more thing, that, in our view, is even more important. On the 31st of August, which means 50 days ago exactly, submitted a motion for exclusion of witnesses under 94 bis. With regard to the witnesses on the list, the Trial Chamber has decided Mr. Donja and Mr. Nielsen, the Defence has submitted a motion to appeal but that has not been decided. Mrs. Hanson should appear before this Court on the side of the Prosecution within several days, and we still don't have a decision about Mr. Hanson [as interpreted]. If the Trial Chamber were to render their ruling today and if that ruling were to be submitted to the parties today, I believe that that fact would have an impact on the integrity of the proceedings and right to a fair trial. Since I have been preparing for Mr. Hanson's cross-examination, I'm even more strongly convinced that our request for the exclusion of that witness was completely justified and for that reason, in case of a negative decision, we're going to request to be able to appeal, and this is going bring to us to quite an unpleasant situation. First of all, we're not going to have the time for the Trial Chamber to look at our certification to appeal in an adequate way and we will still -- we will already have the witness in the courtroom. If there's no decision on the certification to appeal, my approach to the cross-examination of that witness will be interpreted by the Appeals Chamber as the consent of the Defence and our giving up on our certification to appeal, and in that case, the -- any decision on the appeal will be unnecessary from the point of view of the Appeals Chamber. I believe that this jeopardizes the fairness of the trial and the integrity of the proceedings because the Defence is put in a position to act contrary to the interests of its client, because we're not talking about the readiness for the -- of the Defence to cross-examine the witness. The Defence will be ready. We are talking about the situation which goes against the fairness of the trial. I don't see any other way to provide for that. We will be forced to ask for a stay of the proceedings because of the decisions on those matters which will waste additional time. I would like to touch upon another thing which also has an impact on the entire situation, which is, indeed, very worrying. A few days ago, we submitted a request for the exclusion of intercepts and the decision is still pending. Those intercepts are what the alleged expert reports are based on, and a number of them have been tendered into evidence, and that also has to be decided on before the experts enter the courtroom, and a negative decision to that submission will result in the Defence's certification to appeal. I'm not going to deal with all the other pending issues, but I believe that they should be discussed as soon as possible and resolved as soon as possible. Your Honours, we're really very concerned with the developments in the courtroom, as I have already said. I believe that the situation is being worsened by the day, the problems are mounting, and I believe that they have reached a critical stage. We would like to overcome the problems in keeping with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. We want to avoid a situation where the urgency and the time within which the trial has to be brought to an end. We should forget [as interpreted] the rights of the accused that are guaranteed to them by the Statute and the fairness of the trial. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, the Stanisic -- sorry, Zupljanin Defence fully supports the submission of our learned friend, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And one other thing, page 9, 6, instead of "we should forget," "we should not forget." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Oh, sorry, before I hear you, I just want clarification on one point from Mr. Zecevic. The -- your first point about the documents, I'm not sure that I followed the essence of -- of what you are saying there. Do I understand your submission on that point: That the -- well, first of all, are we talking about the same basket of documents that we were dealing with yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, there was three or four documents yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I do understand your submission to be that the method proposed by the Chamber of Defence counselling being permitted to put to the witness the relevant portions on which you rely is inadequate for your purposes. Is that what I understand your position to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. That is exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So what is your specific submission as to how those documents should be dealt with?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the proposal which Defence made yesterday, I tried to explain why, in my submission just a couple of minutes ago, I tried to explain why this is important for us. I hope you understand that. Now, the suggestion by the Defence of yesterday was that the document should be commented by the witness. The document should be MFI'd, waiting for translation, and after translation is -- is received, then the document is offered for exhibit, together with the English translation. That is, I think, the most -- the easiest way. That is how we, with the minimum time, we get what we want and I think it is not -- it is not against the Rules of Procedure or the -- or the practice within this Tribunal. The second option would be that we go and read with the -- with the witness relevant portions, but the problem with that, Your Honour, is that if this document consists of five or six pages, each and every page is a conclusion or a letter sent to somebody, all of that is relevant. So each and every page is relevant. It can be done quickly by the counsel, but it might -- it might take a longer time than -- than the -- than the first alternative that we were talking about. That is -- that is what I say -- what is the essence of my submission. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Zecevic. Yes Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said earlier that Zupljanin Defence fully supports submission of Mr. Zecevic, but it wasn't appearing in the transcript. So it -- just for the record, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Does the -- does Office of the Prosecution have any comment on the submissions made by Mr. Zecevic and supported by Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in respect to the earlier outstanding motions, there are matters that I have raised on a number of different occasions. Let me put it this way: We have said for months now that we really need some resolution on some of the matters. On the intercepts one, however, we do say that was served on us or lodged last week. It's very, very late, indeed, and Mr. Zecevic has been, to my certain knowledge, mentioning this, indeed, on one occasion in a 65 ter conference, and they have waited to the last moment on this one to file a motion. So -- and we have -- 14 -- yes. The report that they included with their motion is dated July the 3rd. So, on this occasion, they are, in our submission, very, very late, and we are going to take the full 14 days that we're entitled to, to deal with that submission. So I don't know what -- what is intended to happen about that. On the other ones, they have been outstanding a very long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As we understand the representations made by Mr. Zecevic, there are, essentially, three points. The first of which relates to the question of these documents, and the Chamber is not unappreciative of the duty of counsel for the Defence in putting forward the case of their respective clients initially by challenging and testing the witnesses called by the Prosecution, even before they would have had a chance to present their case much farther along the road, which fact we would, with respect, remind counsel of that - these proceedings being adversarial - that their chance to present their specific Defence will come. But returning to the difficult question of these documents. The experience of the last part of yesterday indicated that perhaps there is some merit in the Chamber re-visiting its decision as to how these documents should be dealt with, and the -- for the sake of simplicity, we think that -- the documents on which counsel -- which have been dealt with yesterday, that we would go back to that point and have them marked for identification and once the translation is in, we would see where we go, and presumably at some point, having been marked for identification, they would be properly exhibited through the witnesses who are able to -- to deal with them. That seems, to us, to be the only practical way of dealing with these documents. On the matter of the Witness Hanson, the Chamber expects that it will be in a position to give a ruling on that at the close of today's work. In terms of the matter of the question of the intercepts, the -- as counsel for the Prosecution has noted, the time-limits under the Rules are such that the Prosecution has not been in a position to respond, and therefore, a decision on that is premature. But, generally, in terms of the outstanding matters in which the Chamber shares the concern of counsel that these matters appear to be just hanging out there, in our own defence, we must point out that, as with counsel on both sides, the Chamber itself is understaffed, and is -- in addition to staffing problems is, like everybody else, working under pressure of time to conduct the trial while considering the -- these -- these several matters. The matter of -- it may very well be that, to the extent that some of the out-- yet to be resolved objections, in terms of witnesses, and more particularly, the documentation that those witnesses -- that the witness's testimony would carry with them, would necessitate, in order not to delay the progress of the trial, a reconfiguration, for want of a better word, as to how -- as to the order in which witnesses are presented. But that's a day-to-day, situation-by-situation decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, it's not, I'm afraid. Much as we would like to be. We have already reorganised the witness list because of the ban we had. We now have -- we gave the Court a list of witnesses 'till Christmas. We have organised for witnesses to come up already, flights and everything are booked for next week. Intercepts certainly affect some of them. And in respect of Hanson, Mr. Zecevic has very clearly announced that if the rule is in favour of allowing her to testify, then his next move will to be apply for certification to appeal which no doubt we can respond to on the spot on, and that one we can, but it leaves the situation that Ms. Hanson, who is due to start testifying, we thought, maybe tomorrow, but at the rate we're going, probably on Thursday, will not be testifying. So there are all these considerations. Our suggestion was, sometime ago that, of course, the trial should be adjourned while we sorted out all these matters. Your Honours took the view that it was better the trial should start and we've accepted that decision, but we are now in a situation where, to reorganise the witnesses again is going to cause a lot of problems. Because we now have to look at which witnesses are affected by intercepts and which are not, and we have to move Ms. Hanson back again until the matter is dealt with. So it's not quite as simple and straightforward as simply reorganizing the list of the witness. They are all coming from, mainly, from the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We didn't intend to suggest it was simple. We realise there are problems --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I do think that a resolution of the Hanson problem is required, may I say, not at the end of today but now, if possible. Because then we can see where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- when we said at the end of the day, it's after the lunch break that we intend to hand down a decision on Hanson.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour. But -- absolutely. Well, I mean, can I just say this: That if the decision is in favour of the Prosecution being allowed to call, Mr. Zecevic wants to put in a notice to appeal, an application for leave to appeal. Well, that obviously has the effect of her not being able to testify, which will leave a gap. Which, may I say, may not be unuseful for everybody's point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could we have the witness return to the stand. You have something to add, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Witness can enter. In the mean time, I would like just to have a clarification from Trial Chamber. My understanding regarding the admission of -- of documents, the bulk of documents that we spoke yesterday, would we go now through a way of marked for identification, and then at certain stage, as I well understood Your Honour, Judge Hall, that we could tender it through the other witness. I think the proper solution would be the following, and I kindly ask for your instructions. This witness is a highly capable to speak about these documents because he was the creator of these documents and he was a participant in these proceedings. So we have two options. To go through all these documents today with this witness and then once we got official translation, at the moment when we get official translation, it will be admitted as the whole evidence. Whole exhibit. Other solution would be to -- when we get official translation, if we are not following the first avenue, then to call, again, Mr. Delic and to tender through him this, because I don't see other person through whom we could tender these exhibits and probably our friends from OTP will not object to this suggestion. Or maybe they have something to add, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And we have approval from our learned friend, from Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. And may we apologise for all these administrative matters. A couple of matters were raised and we were told that they would only last five minutes this morning, and now so far we have spent more than an hour discussing them. But before we get to you, Judge Delic, let us just clear this last matter and then we will resume the cross-examination. Mr. Zecevic, you suggested that we should re-visit five to six documents which were put to the witness yesterday, and re-visit our determination as to how to deal with this document in terms of admission into evidence. The documents were only in B/C/S and no translation into English seemed to exist. This -- you may remain seated. This is why we suggested that the fastest and easiest way of getting around this was to read out the relevant parts of the documents to the witness and then have him confirm because then we would have the interpretation, or the translation, perhaps, in the record and we could take it from there. Now, you're suggesting that we should re-visit this decision because the remaining parts of those documents, that is to say those parts that were not read out, they also include evidence which is crucial to the Defence, if that is a correct understanding of your observation. The Trial Chamber obviously has no way of discovering this, because we don't read B/C/S and so we have not seen what's in there. But if you insist that they be translated and introduced because you claim that the remaining parts of these documents - I can't recall the number but I think it was five to six documents - if you insist that they include information that the Chamber has to see in order to reach a fair determination of this case, then the Chamber will re-visit its decision. So our ruling is that we kindly ask you to give us the identification numbers of those five to six documents, and we will then MFI them through this witness, and then as soon as we have the translation, we'll get back to it, and we'll make a ruling as to whether they can then be admitted into evidence or not. And that will depend on relevance and probative value. So that's far as the five to six documents go. We will re-visit it and kindly ask you to give to the Registrar the relevant identification numbers. As for the objection raised by Counsel Pantelic, we understood yesterday from the proceedings that Counsel Pantelic wanted to introduce to us a batch of approximately 50 documents for the purpose of showing to the Chamber that all the investigative procedures that had been initiated at the time were done according to the rules, and rather than having to read out the relevant parts of each and every of these documents, we suggested that perhaps the witness could have a look at it overnight and then confirm to us first thing this morning when he starts his -- when he resumes his cross-examination, to confirm to us whether, indeed, his review of those approximately 50 documents - I cannot recall the correct number - had been -- would confirm whether his review of these documents would confirm that the proceedings that had taken place at the time had been done fully in accordance with the rules and regulations that existed then. And we were careful to suggest a precise formulation of the question to be put to the witness yesterday, and it received the approval of both parties. So that is why we thought that, as far as this batch of documents is concerned, a satisfactory procedure would be the one that we suggested; namely, that we ask the witness to have a look at it, and if he can confirm that in all of those instances, the investigations were, indeed, carried out in accordance with the rules and regulations, then that brings an end to that matter. Then the Trial Chamber will accept that, in these cases, the authorities had acted with due diligence and without any discriminatory intent and that is what we asked the witness to confirm, and he is yet to confirm that. We also asked counsel then, in addition to the witness's assessment of the proceedings, or the procedures that had been applied then, to also provide the Chamber with some statistical support in terms of how many incidents do the documents cover; was the perpetrator known; was the victim known; and were there any subsequent judicial proceedings that were initiated as a result of any of the investigations made by the police. So that's where we are. And if parties have no other objections and other matters to raise, I suggest we get on with it, and ask Mr. Pantelic to resume his cross-examination of Judge Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just mention one matter: The statistical matter had -- was something that occurred to us overnight. It's going to take -- because we couldn't talk to the witness or anything like that, it's going to take too long, we feel, to get him to add up the number of cases in the book and then do the various maths. The cases that are represented by those the Defence are going to show him and the ones, indeed, that we've asked him about, are a tiny proportion of what existed in what's called the KT book, so we think that can be done by agreement or possibly through the summary witness, can I put it that way. The second matter is this: If Mr. Pantelic proposes to use with this witness the exhibit that we were provided with, the name marked -- I think it's 2D03-0149, then we've got two pages translated. We got them yesterday. But if that assists there are two pages which are actually translated. So if he gets to that, then we can assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner for this, and I'm sure we will be assisted by seeing those pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, can I proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you hear everything, Mr. Delic? Say "yes" into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I saw you count the number of documents when Judge Harhoff spoke about 50, and you seem to indicate there were less. How many were there? How many are there?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, you have a hawk eye. Actually, it's around 15, it's much less than 50, roughly saying, and while I'm on this topic, I would like to suggest the following method. We already downloaded these documents in e-court and we divided them by titles, and I think it would be fair for my client to follow the same proceedings that Judge Harhoff just suggested, that I can go through Mr. Delic through all these documents, have his comments and his confirmation, if any, then to tender particular documents for MFI, and then, at a certain stage, when we get official translation of these documents, we could have exhibits. If it is so -- if it pleases this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Pantelic. Listen, the Court is not going to tell the Defence how to organise its case. We suggested the procedure yesterday, based exclusively on your own submission that the purpose of bringing these 15 documents to the witness was only to confirm that the proceedings which they cover had been made according to the rules. That was all. And if this is still the case, our suggestion would be that we keep it there. So if the witness now can confirm that everything was done according to the book, fine, that's the end of the matter. If the witness cannot confirm this, then we might wish to go into details and then see which cases were irregular and, in that case, we will perhaps have to consider admission into evidence. But if the witness confirms, as you suggest he would, that everything was done according to the book, as I said, then no question of admission into evidence arises.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will proceed on this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Delic, you had an occasion to look at the documents that were submitted to you by the registry -- did it last night.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you agree that this is a group of documents dealing with certain criminal cases as well as the records of on-site inspections, letters regarding criminal procedures and pre-criminal procedures in Sanski Most during the relevant period which was the year 1992. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As you were studying and perusing the duties, were you able to see that the police did everything in keeping with the law and requests of the prosecutor's office that -- did they do their job in keeping with the law?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see that there were Official Notes for each of the cases, that there were interviews conducted with witnesses in particular cases, and also there are cases where such notes and interview records did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please, can I call up document 2D03-0063.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please look at the first document. I believe that you will find the same number on the right-hand side at the top of the document, 00482336 is the document number. You have it on the screen and you can use that one as well.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is a report against an unknown perpetrator, with the victim being Tehvida Smajlovic. And that case was filed on the 26th of February, 1993. We spoke about it yesterday. The crime happened on the 15th of December, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that case, you as the prosecutor, issued an order to police to carry out some additional actions, and the police, in their turn, filed a criminal report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So as far as this case is concerned, everything was done by the book in keeping with the law?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just bear with me for a moment while I look at the document. There's just a record of the on-site inspection --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Hold on, sir. The time is short. We have to be pragmatic. We have to follow the guide-lines issued by the Trial Chamber. The things are simple. We are not asking for your judgement or your final decision. Since I'm representing my client I'm just asking you - and my client worked in the police not in Sanski Most but at a higher level - what I would like to hear from you, what I would like to know, after the insight into the documents before you, in your view did the police do everything that they were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer whether everything was done as it should have been, because I have nothing to base my conclusion on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Could you please confirm that you issued an order to the police to carry out some additional investigations and interviews, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did the police file a criminal report with regard to this event?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Against an unknown perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was an on-site inspection carried out with regard to this case?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So what is in dispute here? I don't understand you when you say that the police didn't do something that they should have done.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply don't know whether they took statements from eye-witnesses or persons who had information about the incidents -- incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. In this stage, what you have -- you would say that the police did everything as per your instructions.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that stage, yes. But I don't know what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We cannot speculate. This is all we have. Could you please look at the following document, which is 00493238.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is a 2D03-0071. Sorry. It's 00 -- sorry, sorry. It's my mistake. It's a document 2D03-0071.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Delic, this document is three pages long. It's a record of an on-site inspection which was compiled on the 3rd of November, 1992, in the village of Kruhari after the death of nine persons from the village of Skrljevita?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were present?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There was an also an investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And there were also police inspectors on the site?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The bodies were found in the forest called Grahoriste?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnic origin of the people who died?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about these proceedings? Were you in charge of the proceedings since you were on the site? Were perpetrators ever found and arrested?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The perpetrators were found and they were two adults and two minors. The two adults were members of the military at the time, and the criminal report was referred to the military investigative organs. And as far as the minors were concerned, proceedings were conducted before the basic court in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please go to the following page, and you will see number 0048474?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is, in our list, 2D03-0080.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you got the page?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The case was filed on 19 November 1992 against an unknown perpetrator, and the victim was Tade Ilicic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The incident happened on 10th of July, 1992, and the crime in question was a murder; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On page 4 of this case file, under 0048477, it says that you stated that a record of an on-site inspection was received and that you issued certain orders to the police with regard to the incident. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was done in respect of this case; do you remember what happened next?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police filed a criminal report against an unknown perpetrator, and with the report, there was also an Official Note on -- about an interview conducted with the spouse of the deceased. She provided her statement to the police. She said what she knew about the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As the prosecutor in charge, did you issue an indictment against the unknown perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The perpetrator was never identified. Therefore, this is where the process stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that case remained in the KTN long book?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next document it is 00480497.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is 2D03-0080. It is -- I'm calling 2D03-0080.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a file of the 25th of November, 1992, against an unknown perpetrator. The victim is Jose, Galesic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The late Mr. Galesic was a Croat, I believe?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the case there is a criminal report submitted by the police; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next there is a record of an on-site investigation which you attended as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, at a convenient point, we will take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a few seconds, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, towards the end, there are six Official Notes drafted by various police inspectors from Sanski Most; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The police, in this case, pursuant to your order, carried out everything that was necessary; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I think this is a convenient time for break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We will break now and return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We apologise for the delay in taking the Bench, but it was as a result of certain administrative and procedural matters, to facilitate the work -- today's work. One of the things that we have done during the break is to issue a decision, denying the motion for certification to appeal the oral decision accepting Christian Nielsen as an expert and request for a stay of proceedings, so that is in the process of being filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I invite you to resume your cross-examination, and I would point out that you have 1 hour and 26 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will do my best. But just for the record, I'm now -- I'm dealing with a sort of judicial batch of documents which were -- which was provided to us on the October 12th. It was not a part of our strategy for cross-examination before, so due to this reason, I will kindly ask you to adjust, if necessary, time for cross-examination, because, as I said, initially it was not a part of our line, so due to the sort of late disclosure to us, we were -- you know, obliged to tailor our time. So -- but I will do my best to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. As always, let's proceed and we'll see where we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Delic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court 2D03-0094.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, as you can see on the right-hand side corner, upper corner, the number --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic should repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This case file was open on the 23rd of June, 1993, submitted against an unknown perpetrator. The victim is Muhamed Silkic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I apologise my copy is a bit illegible. I believe he is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the file we have a criminal report signed by the police chief, Mirko Vrucinic. In practical terms, it contains a description of the crime, on the 29th of October, 1992, an unknown perpetrator murdered Mr. Muhamed Halkic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next in the file we have an Official Note of the 29th of October by the police inspector, Mr. Mile Dobrijevic from Sanski Most; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next Official Note in the file is the one which, unfortunately, does not have a signature. I suppose this Official Note was also drafted by the police; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Then we have another Official Note which was also drafted by the police. Then there is a third. Something in here seems to have caught my attention. Dejan Bilbija, it seems that his ID was copied. It is contained in the first Official Note, just following the criminal report. What about this Bilbija person, was he a potential suspect or maybe the perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In any case, now I see what it is. Please have a look at page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic should repeat the ERN reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 00482354. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In my opinion in item 5 of this Official Note, it says that in October of 1992 a rifle grenade was fired at the house owned by Dzafe Halilovic. This was stated by a Serb, who said that together with Dusan Bilbija and Darko Miljenovic fired a rifle grenade at the house each. I see an ID photocopy. It says Dejan Bilbija which to me means that the police indeed managed to identify at least one perpetrator, at least one of the suspects.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the actual -- this it actually the police file, a police card of the suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It means that the police made some progress and it turns out that Dejan Bilbija plus an additional two people were suspected of having committed this murder.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the page number 60, which is at the end of the file. There you, as the prosecutor, issued certain orders to the police, to conduct interviews, as well as to undertake other forensic activities, and I believe it was done by the police; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let us next -- let us move to the next criminal file. The last three digits are 378. It is 2D03-0107. This file was opened on the 9th of December, 1992, against an unknown perpetrator. The victim was Petar Pavicic. I suppose his ethnicity was Croatian?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next in the file we have a criminal report submitted by the chief of police in Sanski Most, Mr. Mirko Grucinic [as interpreted] on the 9th of December. It say there that an unknown perpetrator opened automatic -- fire from an automatic weapon, killing Petar Pavicic, after which the perpetrator left the scene of crime in an unknown direction. In the document that we see here, we have your order issued to the police in Sanski Most to undertake certain measures, such as interviews, as well as forensic activities. Next we have document which ends with the three-digit figure of 382. Branko Sobot, who was a police inspector, indeed conducted certain interviews; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It seems that in this file we have all the indications of the police doing their work professionally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I just put -- I have the same problem as the Trial Chamber. I haven't got a translation. Does it say who the perpetrator was alleged to be in this case, in this file?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In this case, actually it was unknown perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. But, yes, but is there a mention of who is suspected of having committed the crime. Perhaps the witness, well --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will try to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Delic, perhaps you can have a look. But as far as I can see from the note of the interview, it cannot be concluded who the perpetrator was. In the letter by the chief of police, which is the document ending in 409, if can you see it, it says that the police issued a dispatch asking that other people be brought in from Prijedor who were members of the 5th Kozara Brigade. Based on that, I conclude that this was probably under the remit of the military prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This concerns another case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, my mistake, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it assists what I'm asking about there seems to be mention of someone called Salko in this file, and I wonder if that's anything to do with it. When I say anything to do with it, the alleged perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. In the criminal report itself, the police say that the unknown perpetrator contacted the spouse of the victim and introduced himself as a Salko. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see from that from the Official Note, following the interview with Marija Pavicic who was the mother of the victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the criminal report, at page 1, you can see what Mr. Grucinic, the chief of police, says. He says that the unknown perpetrator introduced himself as Salko so as to let her know that the murder was committed by a Muslim. We suppose that he was trying to cover up his tracks by trying to pass himself off as a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one can draw that conclusion, since the perpetrator was unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we went through this, in terms of your order to the police, and this was followed through, I believe?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We move to the next document now, which is 2D03-0112. Here we see that the letter by the chief of police, Mirko Grucinic was sent to your prosecutor's office, in relation to the case of Safet Islamovic [phoen] and Osman Muhamodzic [phoen]. These were Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Grucinic says that certain measures were taken and that the two bodies were found as well as that there were indications that the perpetrators were members of the army and of the 5th Kozara Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We can also see here that the police -- well, we don't have the whole file, but I suppose that there followed the legal procedure; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is possible that the police forwarded the file to the military organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We have a note of the scene of crime investigation being undertaken which was standard procedure; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document, which is a crime file opened on the 7th of December, 1992. The last three digits are 439. It is 2D03-0116. This file was open the against an unknown perpetrator who had committed the crime of murder. The victim was Zajneba Alibegovic [phoen] and Zarfije Sinanovic [phoen]from Kijevo. I suppose these two women were Muslim; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the file itself we have what we would usually expect to have there; the murder took place on 6th November, 1992, in the village of Kijevo. As standard procedure you issued an order to the police to undertake certain activities in the pre-trial stage and to conduct interviews. We have there also a report of an on-site investigation. I suppose you were in attendance as well. Next, we have a criminal report, submitted by the chief of police, Mirko Grucinic, with attachments such as statements, gathered by police inspector. In this case, there were at least seven or eight such statements. We can conclude, therefore, that yet again, the police fulfilled all the orders that you issued to them in relation to the case; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next case file ends in 034. It is 2D03-0132 on our list. Mr. Delic, this file was opened on 16th March 1993, submitted against an unknown perpetrator. The victim was Hazema Smajlovic. I suppose she was a Muslim; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next, we have standard correspondence between the prosecutor's office and the police concerning the various orders and what the police were supposed to do. Next, we have a criminal report signed by chief of police, Mirko Grucinic, in which it says that on the 12th September, 1992, there was a blast, an explosion, next to the house owned by a Muslim. On that occasion the owner's wife, Hazema, sustained injuries because of the blast; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We have a report of an on-site investigation as well as an Official Note, actually two, drafted by the police inspector Zdravko Savanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your assessment would you say that everything was done by the police in this case too, by the police in Sanski Most; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next case we have has the last three digits of 042. It is our internal 2D03-04 -- 0140. It was opened on the 17th of February, 1993, submitted against an unknown perpetrator. The victim was Hazim Jakupovic from Kamengrad. I suppose he was Muslim as well?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As part of the file we have the standard correspondence between you and the police by way of orders to the police. We have a criminal report submitted by the chief of police, Mirko Grucinic, in which it says that on the 15th October, 1992, a traffic accident was caused resulting in a fatality, the fatality was Hazim Jakupovic. There's also a record of an on-site investigation which you attended as well. We also have several Official Notes and statements by eye-witnesses. I believe the police also carried out all of your orders; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to the next criminal file, the last three digits are -- is 051. It is our internal number --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll slow down; I apologise. 2D03-0149.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, that's the one we've got translations for, Your Honour, of two pages, which we can put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This a criminal file which was opened on the 15th of March 1993. The perpetrator is unknown, and the victim is Juse Krupic from Donji Kamengrad?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, if Mr. Pantelic waits one second, we'll put up the actual ... Sorry, more than one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It wasn't entered in the transcript that the victim here was most probably of Muslim ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is a criminal report filed by the chief of police at Sanski Most, and it says that on the 11th November, 1992, the body of Juse Krupic was found in a garage of the mosque yard at Donji Kamengrad. And, as part of the criminal report, other evidence is also submitted such as the interview and medical documents, as well as the protocol of the on-site investigation, as well as your correspondence with the police about your orders given to the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, at page 054 of this file --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've got a translation of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We see your letter to the police at Sanski Most, in which you order them to conduct an interview regarding the case of the reserve police officer, Zoran Miladinovic, would focus on the circumstances --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat this part of his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the Prosecutor [sic] didn't hear your question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The interpreter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The interpreter, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So let me repeat. In your letter dated 8 December, 1992, which you sent to the police at Sanski Most, you issue an order to conduct an interview about the case of the reserve police officer, a certain Zoran Miladinovic, focussing on the circumstances when and why and which way he took the deceased person who was the duty officer with him at the check-point and all other circumstances the police needs to know about. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, it is obvious that here, too, in a way, a police officer was involved in the activities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At any rate, this criminal file includes your orders, as well as the protocol of the on-site investigation, where it is established that a police officer, too, was involved in the event; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know how this case developed subsequently? Did the police officer conduct an internal inquiry, or did he launch a procedure following your orders?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now whether the perpetrator was found, whether a person was actually reported as a perpetrator of this criminal act.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. But certainly in the criminal report that we see here, we see that following your orders interviews were conducted with Zoran Miladinovic, a police officer, isn't that correct, on page 1, and with other persons of whom we don't know now whether they were police officers or eye-witnesses. But your orders were followed, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the criminal report says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next file we want to look at now has the last three digits of 526. Our internal mark is 2D03-0158. This is a criminal file which was opened on the 14th of September, 1992, against an unknown perpetrator. And the victim was Alma Kicin, a minor from Demisevac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I suppose that the victim was of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the following page we can see your orders to the police. That's the usual correspondence. And there is also a criminal report filed by the chief of police, Mirko Vrucinic, which says -- or which states that during the night between the 3rd and the 4th of December, 1992, one perpetrator or several shot from the dark at the house owned by a Muslim, and on that occasion, the victim, the minor victim Alma was killed. And the protocol of the on-site investigation and the interviews conducted following your office are also included. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So in this case, too, we can say that the police followed the procedure, in accordance with your order; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now there's another document which has a number. It follows from this one - the last three digits are 820 - and that's your letter that you sent to the police. It is dated the 13th of August. It's on the next page following this file, the file about this girl Alma. Sorry, no, my mistake. No. It's a separate set of documents. The number is 998, yes, we do have that one. And then the -- followed by 999. And then 820. We don't have the criminal files here, but this is the correspondence in which you give orders to the police, but that is not relevant now. This is the 1st of July, 1994. Although, the KTA [as interpreted] is 11392, but this event is from 1992, right; and the correspondence followed later?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that some police activities took place, and the unknown perpetrators from 1992 seem to have been located, and it was established that they are members of the 6th Kozara Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your next letter also has to do with a case where the victims were Muslims and where you also gave orders to the police. It is about some events and an on-site investigation done on the 8th of November, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You give an order here and inform the police that it is required, should some -- should they learn of some information that they inform you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next file was opened on the 13th of August, 1992, where you sent a letter to the police, dated the 13th of August. And you say that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, my mistake. [Interpretation] 2D03-0168. This is just a single document --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- where you inform the police of Sanski Most that they should collect the necessary information concerning the protocol of the on-site investigation made on the 13th of August which we don't have here. But, as far as I can tell, some incident seems to have happened and it was necessary for the police to follow the regular procedure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is a case which you spoke about yesterday to my learned friend, Mr. Cvijetic. It is rather comprehensive. It's 2D03-0169 and we won't dwell on it here, but we can say that it is a complete criminal file, including a criminal report which was submitted against known perpetrators of Serb ethnicity who had committed the crime of murder at Stari Majdan and that individual or the group, if you remember, killed those two Muslims, right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an individual perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, an individual. And he was a member of the 6th Krajina Brigade, and then the military prosecutor took over and it was further processed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Right. We established that yesterday. But we can also see that the police did everything that was necessary and that they had the authority to do following your orders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let us proceed with the next set of documents, the first one with the last three digits being 862. Our document number is 2903-0241. Then 42, 43, 44, 46, 48, 52, 54, and 57. Let's not go into details now, but we can establish that these are on-site investigation protocols concerning various events, the first one is dated 15th of June, 1992. You were also present as well as -- or, rather, as a member of the member of the police of Sanski Most. A dead body was found in the Sana river, and the required forensic activities were conducted and procedures followed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next one is also dated 15th of June. You were present. Also an on-site investigation protocol in the Sana river -- let me just check. Yes, it was on the same day but another investigation. A dead body was found and the procedure was followed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Then the next one is an on-site investigation done on the 17th of August, where the late Munib Masic was found, a Muslim, I suppose. I am speaking about the document dated 17 August 1992. It should be in this sequence. The number in the upper corner is 880.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is also part of the procedure that you conducted with the police on the 17th of August, 1992, when a dead body -- the dead body of a Muslim, Munib Masic, was found, and the forensic procedure was conducted. Let us now pass to the following document, dated the 27th of August, 1992. It is also an on-site investigation protocol. The police, a medical doctor, and the prosecution were present. Four bodies were found, and the regular procedure was conducted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just explain. We received information about four dead bodies from the village of Kljevci, but we didn't find the bodies at the site. There was a report about the dead body of Petar Ivankovic. We commented that case already with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. The next on-site investigation protocol was compiled on 13th of September, 1992, again, in the presence of both the prosecutor's office and the police as well as the forensic expert --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just mention that Mr. Pantelic is not actually giving the exhibits any numbers at the moment. He's just going straight through. I don't mind, but if he wants later for reference, the D numbers are not coming out, unless you propose to do the whole as a bulk exhibit at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my initial idea, but let's hear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think the idea behind this approach was not to have these documents exhibited because the purpose of this exercise was only to discover, whether according to the witness, the procedures that were taken and the measures that were taken to investigate those crimes were taken correctly, according to the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I quite understand that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So if the witness, by the end of this exercise, is able to assess the quality of the measures taken for investigation and -- and perhaps prosecution, then that would be the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. At the moment, Mr. Pantelic is, in fact, he's just going on different dates, but what is not altogether clear is that these are actually separate files. He was giving the numbers originally but he stopped, and so at the moment purely for later purposes, if necessary, I -- if Mr. Pantelic -- if they're going to be exhibited, is going to put them as one bulk, that's one thing. It doesn't really matter. But at the moment it is very difficult to see, from reading the transcript, that he is actually referring to different perpetrator files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, apparently you have been giving reference numbers to the files that you have introduced so far except for the last two ones, so maybe you would be good enough to continue the practice, just said, so as to enable the Chamber, in the end, if we have to considered admission of any of these documents, we can then identify them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will do that gladly. Your Honour, my initial idea was just to cover all these separate activities of police and prosecution and then to have Mr. Delic opinion but no problem; although, again, the most preferable way for us would be that we could tender all these documents and then have [indiscernible] I'm repeating, you know, [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... like Cato in Rome that Carthage should be destroyed by Rome, don't understand me wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let's see about that when we get to the end of this exercise, but can I just, for clarification, ask you to indicate the number of files, because when Judge Delvoie asked you a while ago how many documents we were talking about, you said 15 documents. But it seems to me that we have far exceeded the number of 15 documents, and I wonder if what you meant to say was that the batch consists of 15 files and each file would then consist of a number of subdocuments so to say. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, actually, my information was that actually we are speaking about the number of files but with many documents, but, of course, I covered with -- with Mr. Delic when I speak about one case, one file, we covered many, many pages. So in total, we have around roughly 15, plus we have now this particular on-site records, which my idea was to cover all together, but will follow your instruction, Your Honour, and I think it's absolutely appropriate. So to go back --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to say for the sake of the procedure that the document you have before you displaying the last two digits 862 is actually 2D03-0241. We have already spoken about this document. This is an on-site investigation protocol dated 15 June, dealing with the body in the Sana. And the next document is your number 863 and it is our number 2D03-0242, another on-site investigation protocol drafted on the same date, and it seems to me that it was drafted maybe an hour or so later. Again, dealing with the body in the river Sana.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next on-site investigation protocol bears the last three digits 880, and it is ours 2D03-0243. And this is an on-site investigation protocol dated 17 August 1992. A body -- the body of Munib Basic [as interpreted], a Muslim was found, and the procedure was carried out and an on-site investigation protocol drafted.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is 2D03-0244, and your number is 882. This is an on-site investigation protocol that you also attended on the 27th of August, 1992, or maybe 29th of August -- no, I believe it's the 27th of August, 1992. We have already spoken about that. In the village of Kljevci three female and one male bodies were found; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had information that there were four bodies. However, we did not find the bodies on the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is 2D03-02446. This is another on-site investigation protocol drafted on the 13th of September, 1992. An explosion had taken place in the village of -- this is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Husimovci [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Husimovci. And the prosecutor and the police attended the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And there were also casualties, as can I see. We've already said that. They were all Muslim, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then we have the next document which is under our internal number 2D03-0248, and your number is 886. This is an on-site investigation protocol dated 18 September 1992, again, in the presence of the prosecutor, the police, and the court expert, a forensic medical expert. The case was probably a murder case. The information is contained in here. The protocol was compiled, and the victim was a Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And, again, a certain legal procedure was applied involving the prosecutor and the police; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document we have is 2D03-0252. This is an on-site investigation protocol dated 18 September --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Hold on a minute, Mr. Pantelic. Can we just go back to the previous document and your question to the witness was, and I quote from what is on my screen, page 46, line 3, your question was: "Again, certain legal procedures was applied involving the prosecutor and the police; right?" And the witness answers: "Right." Can you elicit with the witness what were the legal procedures taking?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, you heard His Honour, Judge Harhoff. Could you please explain the nature of the procedure that was applied and involved the prosecutor, the police, and an investigating judge at the moment of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The body was found and the investigating judge, the policemen, the crime technician, the physician and I, myself, went to the site, and the investigation was headed by the investigative judge, with the participation of crime technician, forensic technician, and inspector, and the investigating judge compiled the protocol describing the site and what was found on the site.
